name: Secrets
tagline: An Azure Key Vault with synthetic secrets, keys that really sign, certificates and a log of every read.
point: https://<vault>.vault.<env base domain>:8444 (trust the Stuntman Test CA)
the Azure SDK as is: SecretClient, KeyClient, CertificateClient

capabilities.title: Secrets with versions
capabilities.text: Synthetic values with versions, expiry, content type and tags. A new version sends SecretNewVersionCreated to subscribers.

capabilities.title: Keys that really sign
capabilities.text: RSA 2048, 3072 or 4096 keys that sign, verify, wrap and unwrap, so the app's crypto code runs for real.

capabilities.title: Certificates from a Test CA
capabilities.text: Issue, import (.pfx or PEM) and renew certificates; each shows subject, issuer, validity and days left.

capabilities.title: Who reads what
capabilities.text: Reads per process and per identity. A secret read on every request shows up at once: the app is not caching it.

capabilities.title: An access log
capabilities.text: Every operation with identity, item and answer, kept 24 h, and vault_patterns lists what looks wrong.

capabilities.title: Managed identity
capabilities.text: The IMDS token endpoint hands tokens to identities with roles and name scopes, like Key Vault RBAC.

capabilities.title: What a real vault refuses
capabilities.text: With any_token on, would_fail lists the operations a real vault would have refused for that identity.

capabilities.title: Soft delete and recover
capabilities.text: Deleted items stay soft-deleted: recreating the name gets 409 until recover_item.

capabilities.title: Find every reference
capabilities.text: secret_used_by lists the environment files that point at secret://<name>, even before the secret exists.

callouts.title: Read 2,140 times
callouts.text: Reads in the last hour per secret; a big number means the app reads it on every request.

callouts.title: Versions
callouts.text: Current, disabled or expired versions, each with its own read count.

callouts.title: Who reads it
callouts.text: Each process and identity, and whether it looks cached.

callouts.title: Next reads
callouts.text: Make the next reads fail: 403, 404, disabled, 429 or slow.

callouts.title: Rotate
callouts.text: A new version and SecretNewVersionCreated to subscribers.

callouts.title: Worth a look
callouts.text: A pattern found in the log: a secret read on every request, which a real vault would throttle.

callouts.title: Refused
callouts.text: 403 for an identity without the role for this item.

callouts.title: Unknown caller
callouts.text: A request with no known identity gets 401, and is listed.

callouts.title: The caller
callouts.text: Identity, object id and role of the token that made the call.

callouts.title: Pattern
callouts.text: Same secret, same process, 2 ms apart: the app has no cache.

callouts.title: Operations
callouts.text: Sign, verify, wrap and unwrap in the last hour, with p95.

callouts.title: Real crypto
callouts.text: Signatures verify with the public key; wrapped keys unwrap again.

callouts.title: Next operations
callouts.text: Disabled, 403, 429, slow, or a wrong signature that fails verify.

callouts.title: Versions
callouts.text: Rotation adds a version; signatures from the older one still verify.

callouts.title: Public key
callouts.text: As JWK or PEM, to verify outside the app.

provoke.name: Secret disabled
provoke.what: Reads answer as for a disabled secret

provoke.name: Wrong signature
provoke.what: sign returns a signature that fails verify

provoke.name: Certificate expired
provoke.what: Expired, not yet valid, missing or untrusted

provoke.name: IMDS fails
provoke.what: The token endpoint answers 500, slow or no identity

advantages.title: No real values
advantages.text: Values are synthetic, so tests and agents never touch a production secret or a cloud subscription.

advantages.title: Caching made visible
advantages.text: Read counts per process prove whether the app caches secrets, which the real vault only shows as throttling later.

advantages.title: Failures on request
advantages.text: Expired certificates, wrong signatures and a broken IMDS happen on the next call, not on the day they expire.

advantages.title: Real crypto, no HSM
advantages.text: Keys really sign and wrap, so signing code is tested end to end without a vault in Azure.

agent.prompt: Find out whether the app caches the HMAC signing secret or reads it on every request.
steps: signing-hmac-key read on every request by acme-api
tools: Secrets with version, state, expiry and reads
A new version of a synthetic secret
Who read a secret and whether it looks cached
Make key operations fail or sign wrongly
What a real vault would have refused

notes: The vault is found by host name: give each environment a base domain under a wildcard DNS name.
